observation_summary: The BOBYQAOptimizer was throwing a 'PathIsExploredException' when the number of interpolation points exceeded 2*dim+1, and the code contained incorrect index calculations (off-by-one errors) when accessing interpolation points.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved removing artificial exception-throwing guards that were blocking valid execution paths and correcting the index calculation logic (ipt-1, jpt-1) used to access the interpolation points array. These are procedural/algorithmic corrections to the data access logic within the 'prelim' method, rather than simple value assignments or missing guards.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the removal of 'throw new PathIsExploredException()' which was blocking execution.
The fix_diff_oracle shows the correction of index variables 'iptMinus1' and 'jptMinus1' from 'ipt'/'jpt' to 'ipt-1'/'jpt-1'.
The bug report mentions an off-by-one error in the translation from FORTRAN.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix removed an exception throw (a guard), the root cause was the incorrect index calculation logic that necessitated the exception in the first place.
The fix involves changing the logic of how indices are calculated and used in array access, which is more complex than a simple incorrect constant or variable initialization.
